correctness.rationale: For X=Ind_2(GP(10,2)), all selected induced degrees <=1. Direct independent enumeration of all 2^20 masks yielded 63,143 faces including empty and f-vector (-1 through11) 1,20,190,1080,3985,9772,15870,16640,10770,4000,750,60,5. Independently reconstructed full pivot-toggle matching and oriented 410,500-cover Hasse DAG: 31,565 disjoint pairs, complete topological sort on 63,142 nonempty faces, critical cells one 0, one 5, six 6 and four 7. Independently computed exact signed integral Morse boundaries ∂6=[0,0,-1,0,1,0] and ∂7 with columns (1,0,0,0,0,0),(1,0,1,-1,1,0),(0,0,0,1,0,-1),(0,-1,0,0,0,0); first four rows of ∂7 have determinant ±1. Thus ∂6 surjects and ∂7 injects with primitive image, H6=Z, other reduced integral homology zero. The Morse CW model has no dimensions 1..4, then vanishing H5 forces π5=0 by Hurewicz, and a map from S6 inducing H6 iso is a homotopy equivalence by simply connected homological Whitehead: X≃S6, no torsion inference from mod2 alone. Independent signed fixed-face calculation for central antipode on all face masks gave reduced Lefschetz -1; the rotation subgroup A5 has no nontrivial rank-one characters, yielding antipodal sign on H6 for full A5×C2. This is finite exact enumeration with proof of exhaustiveness, not a sampled conjecture.

originality.rationale: The published same-graph dodecahedral Ind(D) computation gives wedge of four S5 spheres, but Ind_2(D) is a different complex with 63,142 rather than ~5,827 nonempty faces and S6. Graph-matching, neighborhood, Čech, Rips, configuration-space published records also use different face predicates; higher-independence family theorems in Deshpande--Singh and Sawant cover trees, cycles and multipartite, not this cubic dodecahedral graph. Best-of-knowledge the present exact integral homotopy and antipodal module are new, with possible unindexed overlap risk.

value.rationale: The regular dodecahedral graph is a canonical Platonic graph; obtaining an actual S6 despite an eleven-dimensional nonpure two-independence complex is a nontrivial finite homotopy classification, and antipodal sign on integral top homology is a natural symmetry invariant. Future graph-complex comparisons could use this exact benchmark. No downstream theorem requirement is imposed.
